learning: If max_error stays near 0.062 m with kp 4 and kd 0.6, the bend speed is the limit, not the gains, so the next change is base_speed. If steering_oscillation rises sharply, kp 4 is too high and kd should go up instead.
notes: Builder's lag and inertia change (y 0.02, body 0.14 m, mass 0.7 kg) with a stiffer controller (kp 4.0, kd 0.6) to cut the 0.062 m max_error. Other controller values unchanged to isolate the gain change.
rationale: Race evidence from iteration 1 (entityR2B, 111.8 score). Line loss fell from 1 to 0 events on oval and s-bend and to 0.1 on slalom, so the wider 0.06 m span solved sensing. Every run still ended off_track, with max_error at 0.062 to 0.064 m against the 0.06 m limit and rms_error steady at 0.026 to 0.029 m. Steering oscillation is low (0.13 to 0.27), so the controller is not oscillating. It is tracking too loosely, and it is reacting late: slalom progress is only 0.10. The Builder's geometry for this iteration shortens the sensor-to-axle lag (y 0.03 to 0.02) and cuts yaw inertia about 20 percent, which should help. I have kept the Builder's geometry unchanged, so this race isolates the controller change. For the controller I raise kp from 3.0 to 4.0 to tighten tracking and cut the rms and max error, and I raise kd from 0.3 to 0.6 to damp the extra gain and the phase lag. I keep ki at 0.05 because there is no sign of a steady-state offset, and I keep base_speed at 1.2 because the failures are off-track drift, not a lack of speed. Sensor weights stay at -2 to +2 to match the new 0.03 m spacing. line_loss stays last_direction, which is working. Expected result: max_error below 0.06 m on more trials and lower rms_error. If max_error still sits near 0.062 m with the higher gain, the limit is the speed on the bends, and I will lower base_speed next iteration.
